desc: Generate interactive event markers where each row is a clickable marker, optionally filtered by a boolean column. Click an event marker to navigate to that timestamp on the candlestick chart. Columns in schema map to inputs by position.

name: Futures Continuation

options.name: Rollover Method
options.desc: Method for detecting when to roll from front to back contract. FirstOfMonth rolls on the 1st trading day of the expiry month. LastTradingDay rolls N days before the last trading day. LiquidityBased rolls when back contract volume exceeds front.
options.tuningGuidance: FirstOfMonth is the most common. Use LastTradingDay with an offset for contracts that lose liquidity before expiry. LiquidityBased is data-adaptive but requires volume data.

options.name: Adjustment Method
options.desc: Price adjustment method to eliminate gaps between contracts. NoAdjustment passes raw prices through without adjustment. BackwardPanamaCanal adjusts historical prices by absolute difference. BackwardRatio adjusts by ratio (preserves returns). Forward variants adjust future prices instead of historical.
options.tuningGuidance: BackwardPanamaCanal is standard for most strategies. Use BackwardRatio when percentage returns matter more than levels. Forward methods are less common but avoid changing historical data. NoAdjustment for raw unadjusted continuation.

options.name: Roll Offset Days
options.desc: Number of days offset for rollover. For LastTradingDay, rolls N days before the last trading day. For FirstOfMonth, shifts the roll date.
options.tuningGuidance: 0 is standard. Increase to 1-5 for illiquid contracts that need earlier rolls to avoid slippage.

options.name: Spread Depth
options.desc: Compute calendar spread between front month and the Nth deferred contract. 0 = disabled (no spread output). 1 = front vs 2nd nearby, 2 = front vs 3rd nearby, etc. Spread = front.close - deferred.close (positive = backwardation, negative = contango). Use AdjustmentType.NoAdjustment for meaningful spread values.
options.tuningGuidance: 2 is the most common (front vs 3rd nearby). Use 1 for near-term tightness, 11 for full curve slope. NaN when deferred contract is unavailable.

desc: Builds continuous futures price series from individual contracts. Detects rollover dates using the specified rollover method and applies price adjustments to eliminate gaps between contracts.
usageContext: Use as the data source for futures strategies. Access via outputs: cont.o (open), cont.h (high), cont.l (low), cont.c (close), cont.v (volume), cont.oi (open interest), cont.s (active contract symbol), cont.dte (days to expiry of current front contract). Use cont.dte for proper annualization: annualized_basis = basis * (365 / cont.dte).
limitations: Requires multiple futures contracts loaded for the same root asset. Raw contract data must include a CONTRACT column identifying each contract.

name: IPOs
desc: IPO event data for quant analysis. Index is listing_date. Use for IPO pop (first-day return), deal size factors, and event studies. Filter by ipo_status='history' for completed IPOs.
usageContext:
IPO listing data including pricing, offer size, and status.
- IPO pop analysis: Compare final_issue_price to first-day close.
- Deal size screening: Use total_offer_size for capital-raising magnitude.
- Pipeline monitoring: Track pending, rumor, and withdrawn IPOs.
Combine with price data for post-IPO performance studies.
limitations:
Sparse: Typically 1 row per ticker (the listing event). NullPolicy=AllowAll.
Coverage: From 2008 onward.
Only ipo_status='history' has finalized pricing. Pending/rumored IPOs may have null final_issue_price.

name: Inverse Volatility Weight

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights, applied iteratively)

options.name: Minimum Volatility
options.desc: Volatility floor to prevent low-vol assets from dominating. E.g., 0.05 means any asset with <5% vol is treated as having 5% vol. Set to 0 to disable.

desc: Cross-sectional allocator that assigns weights inversely proportional to volatility. Higher volatility assets get lower weights. Formula: w_i = (1/vol_i) / sum(1/vol_j). Provides natural risk balancing without complex optimization. Use min_volatility to prevent very low-vol assets from dominating the portfolio.
usageContext: inv_vol_weight(active_mask=cs_rank(momentum)<=10, volatility=return_vol(20), min_volatility=0.05). Lower vol assets get higher weights for risk balancing. Use min_volatility to prevent money-market or very stable assets from dominating. Connect weight output to dynamic_size(type='percent') for sizing.
limitations: Cross-sectional only. Requires volatility input. Zero or negative volatility assets are excluded. Without min_volatility, very low-vol assets may get extreme weights.

name: Risk Parity

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)

options.name: Max Iterations
options.desc: Maximum iterations for Newton optimization

options.name: Tolerance
options.desc: Convergence tolerance

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights)

desc: Equal Risk Contribution (ERC) portfolio where each asset contributes equally to total risk. Uses rolling estimation with configurable rebalance frequency. Uses Newton iteration to solve: RC_i = w_i * (Sigma*w)_i / port_vol = 1/N for all i. Reference: Maillard, Roncalli, Teiletche (2010).
usageContext: risk_parity(returns=pct_change(close), lookback=252). Each asset contributes equally to portfolio risk. Connect weight output to dynamic_size(type='percent') for sizing.
limitations: Cross-sectional only. Requires sufficient lookback for stable covariance. May not converge for highly correlated assets.

name: Lowest Bars

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback period to search for lowest value
options.tuningGuidance: 260 for 52-week low, 20 for monthly low

desc: Returns how many bars ago the lowest value occurred within the lookback period. 0 means current bar is the low (new low / breakdown). Negative values indicate bars ago (-5 = low was 5 bars ago).
usageContext: Pine Script ta.lowestbars() equivalent. Detect how recently a new low was made — lowestbars == 0 means new low on current bar. Use for support detection: lowestbars(low, 260) == 0 detects 52-week lows. Mirror of highestbars for bearish setups and capitulation detection.
limitations: Returns NA for first (period-1) bars. Only tracks the most recent lowest — does not capture multiple lows within the lookback.

name: Hierarchical Equal Risk Contribution

options.name: Linkage Method
options.desc: Clustering linkage method: single, complete, average, ward

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)

options.name: Max Clusters
options.desc: Maximum number of clusters to consider

options.name: Risk Measure
options.desc: Risk measure: variance, vol

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights)

desc: Hierarchical Equal Risk Contribution extends HRP by finding optimal clusters and ensuring equal risk contribution between clusters. Allocates inter-cluster by inverse risk and intra-cluster by inverse variance. Reference: Riskfolio-Lib.
usageContext: herc(returns=pct_change(close), linkage='ward', max_k=10). Combines HRP clustering with equal risk contribution. Connect weight output to dynamic_size(type='percent') for sizing.
limitations: Cross-sectional only. More computationally intensive than HRP. Optimal k selection may be sensitive to market conditions.

name: Minimum Variance

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset

desc: Minimum Variance portfolio minimizes total portfolio volatility. Uses rolling estimation with configurable rebalance frequency. Finds weights that minimize w'Σw subject to sum(w)=1, w>=0. Does not require expected return estimates.
usageContext: min_variance(returns=pct_change(close), lookback=252). Lowest volatility portfolio on efficient frontier. Connect weight output to dynamic_size(type='percent') for sizing.
limitations: Cross-sectional only. May concentrate in low-vol assets. Sensitive to covariance estimation errors.

name: Minimum CVaR

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for estimation

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)

options.name: Confidence Level
options.desc: CVaR confidence level (e.g., 0.05 = 5% worst cases)

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset

desc: Minimum CVaR (Conditional Value at Risk, Expected Shortfall) portfolio minimizes expected loss in the worst α% of scenarios. Better captures tail risk than variance.
usageContext: min_cvar(returns=pct_change(close), alpha=0.05). Minimizes expected loss in worst 5% of scenarios. Connect weight output to dynamic_size(type='percent') for sizing.
limitations: Cross-sectional only. Requires sufficient history for tail estimation. More computationally intensive than variance-based methods.

name: Black-Litterman

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)

options.name: Prior Uncertainty
options.desc: Uncertainty scalar for prior (typically 0.025-0.05)

options.name: Risk Aversion
options.desc: Market risk aversion coefficient

options.name: Annualization Factor
options.desc: Factor to annualize returns

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset

desc: Black-Litterman model combines market equilibrium with investor views using Bayesian inference. This simplified version blends equilibrium returns with historical returns for more stable estimates.
usageContext: black_litterman(returns=pct_change(close), tau=0.05). Shrinks returns toward equilibrium for stability. Connect weight output to dynamic_size(type='percent') for sizing.
limitations: Cross-sectional only. Simplified version without explicit views. Full BL requires view matrix specification.

name: Minimum Semivariance

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for estimation

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)

options.name: Benchmark Return
options.desc: Benchmark return for downside calculation (typically 0)

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset

desc: Minimum Semivariance portfolio minimizes downside risk only, ignoring upside volatility. Uses semicovariance matrix computed from returns below the benchmark.
usageContext: min_semivariance(returns=pct_change(close), benchmark=0). Minimizes downside volatility only. Connect weight output to dynamic_size(type='percent') for sizing.
limitations: Cross-sectional only. Requires sufficient negative return observations. Semicovariance matrix may be less stable than full covariance.

name: Donchian Channel

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Lookback period for highest high and lowest low
options.tuningGuidance: Classic Turtle Trading uses 20 for entry, 10 for exit. Shorter periods (10-15) for more responsive but noisier breakout signals. Longer periods (50-55) for capturing larger trend moves.

desc: Price channel formed by the highest high and lowest low over a rolling window, with a middle line at the average. Used in the famous Turtle Trading system. Breakout above the upper channel signals potential uptrend; below the lower channel signals potential downtrend.
usageContext: Classic breakout channel used in the Turtle Trading system (Richard Dennis, 1983). The upper band is the N-period highest high, lower band is the N-period lowest low. Breakouts beyond these extremes signal new trends. KEY RULES (Turtle Trading): (1) Enter long when price breaks above 20-day high (upper channel). (2) Enter short when price breaks below 20-day low (lower channel). (3) Exit on 10-day channel break in opposite direction. CHANNEL WIDTH: Narrowing channels indicate decreasing volatility - breakout imminent. Wide channels indicate high volatility - strong trend or whipsaw risk. PIPELINE PATTERN: (1) Compute Donchian(20) for entry signals, (2) compute Donchian(10) for exit signals, (3) enter on upper channel breakout, (4) exit when price hits 10-day lower channel. KEY DIFFERENCE from Bollinger Bands: Donchian uses actual price extremes (high/low) rather than standard deviations from a moving average. More robust to distribution assumptions, directly captures breakout levels. EXAMPLES: (1) Turtle entry: Price makes new 20-day high = enter long. Trail stop at 10-day low. (2) Squeeze detection: Channel width (upper - lower) at multi-month minimum signals impending volatility expansion. (3) Range trading: In sideways markets, buy at lower channel, sell at upper channel.
limitations: Lagging by definition - only signals after the breakout has occurred. The famous Turtle system had 60%+ losing trades but large winners compensated. Requires strict position sizing to survive losing streaks. Middle line is simple average of extremes, not a moving average - can be jumpy. Channel width depends entirely on the single most extreme bar in the window.

name: Trade Count
desc: Number of trades per bar (provider 'n').
usageContext: Use to gauge liquidity and detect unusual activity. Spikes in trade count relative to average (percentrank > 90) indicate institutional activity or news events. Combine with volume for participation rate analysis: high volume + low trade count = large block orders.
limitations: Depends on provider aggregation — tick-level vs trade-level counting varies by data source. Not available from all providers. Not available for futures — futures data providers do not supply per-bar trade count.

name: Basic Volatility

options.name: Volatility Type
options.desc: Type of volatility calculation

options.name: Period
options.desc: Rolling window size for standard deviation calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Shorter periods (10-14) track volatility changes quickly but are noisier. Standard 20 for daily data (~1 month). Longer periods (60-90) for stable estimates.

desc: Rolling standard deviation of close price changes. Return type calculates volatility of percentage returns (comparable across assets). Price difference type calculates dollar volatility.
usageContext: Use return type for standard volatility (Sharpe ratio, VaR, cross-asset comparison). OUTPUT SCALE (return type): Decimal standard deviation of returns, NOT multiplied by 100. Typical values ~0.01-0.05 for daily bars. Use price_diff type for dollar-based position sizing (output in price units). For more efficient OHLC-based estimation, use volatility_estimator.
limitations: Only uses close prices - doesn't capture intraday volatility. For OHLC-based estimators, use volatility_estimator (garman_klass, yang_zhang, etc.).

name: Price Distance
desc: Measures the normalized price distance using OHLC data. Computes a composite distance metric from open, high, low, and close prices, useful for detecting unusual price movement patterns and market activity levels.
usageContext: Measure normalized price movement intensity from OHLC bar structure. Uses the HosseinMoein DataFrame pdist visitor to compute a composite distance metric from open, high, low, and close relationships. TYPICAL USES: (1) Activity filter: High price distance indicates unusual market activity - potential breakout or news event. Low values indicate quiet, range-bound conditions. (2) Volatility proxy: Correlates with realized volatility but captures intra-bar dynamics that close-to-close volatility misses. (3) Bar quality assessment: Filter out bars with abnormally low or high distance before feeding to other indicators. PIPELINE PATTERN: Compute price_distance, then use zscore to normalize it. High z-score (>2) flags unusual activity bars for breakout detection.
limitations: No configurable parameters - uses fixed OHLC relationship formula. Interpretation depends on the asset's typical bar structure. Less meaningful on very short timeframes where bid-ask spread dominates the OHLC range. No explicit volume consideration.

name: Market Facilitation Index
desc: Market Facilitation Index. Measures market readiness to move prices with minimal volume.
usageContext: Ratio of price range to volume - measures price movement efficiency. High MFI + high volume = strong trend (green). High MFI + low volume = fake move (fade). Low MFI + high volume = churning (distribution/accumulation). Low MFI + low volume = squat (buildup before breakout). PIPELINE PATTERN: classify each bar by MFI/volume combination for market state analysis.
limitations: Requires manual classification of MFI+volume combinations. Raw values vary significantly across instruments. Less standardized than other volume indicators. Best used as a bar-by-bar classifier, not as a continuous oscillator.

name: Aroon Oscillator
desc: Aroon Oscillator. Subtracts Aroon Down from Aroon Up, measuring the strength of a prevailing trend.
usageContext: Single-line version of Aroon: Aroon Up minus Aroon Down. Range -100 to +100. Positive = uptrend (recent highs more recent than lows), negative = downtrend. Magnitude indicates trend strength. PIPELINE PATTERN: compute aroonosc(), use > 50 for strong uptrend filter, < -50 for strong downtrend. EXAMPLE: aroonosc crossing above zero = trend direction shifting bullish.
limitations: Simplified version of Aroon - loses the detail of individual Up/Down lines. Can hover near zero in ranging markets producing no clear signals. Based solely on time since highs/lows, ignoring price magnitude. Default 25 period.

name: Elder's Market Thermometer

options.name: Period
options.desc: EMA period for smoothing the thermometer reading
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 22 (approximately one month). Shorter periods for more responsive readings. Longer for smoother trend assessment.

options.name: Buy Factor
options.desc: Multiplier for generating buy signals relative to the EMA
options.tuningGuidance: Default 0.1. Lower values generate fewer but more selective buy signals.

options.name: Sell Factor
options.desc: Multiplier for generating sell signals relative to the EMA
options.tuningGuidance: Default 0.5. Higher values require more extreme readings for sell signals.

desc: Elder's Market Thermometer measures the true range activity of the market and compares it to an EMA for signal generation. Developed by Alexander Elder. Outputs the raw thermometer reading, its EMA, and buy/sell signals based on configurable factors relative to the smoothed reading.
usageContext: Measure market 'temperature' - the level of price activity relative to recent history. Developed by Alexander Elder as part of his Triple Screen trading system. KEY INTERPRETATION: High thermometer reading (above EMA) = hot market, active trading. Low reading (below EMA) = cool market, consolidation. The buy and sell signals are generated when the thermometer reading crosses above/below factor thresholds relative to the EMA. PIPELINE PATTERN: (1) Compute Elder's Thermometer, (2) when thermometer drops below EMA * buy_factor = market cooling, look for mean-reversion entries at support. (3) When thermometer spikes above EMA * sell_factor = market overheating, consider taking profits or tightening stops. KEY DIFFERENCE from ATR: While ATR measures absolute volatility, Elder's Thermometer compares current activity to its own recent average (EMA) and generates explicit buy/sell signals. The asymmetric factors (buy=0.1, sell=0.5) reflect that quiet markets often precede breakouts (buy) while hot markets often precede corrections (sell). EXAMPLES: (1) Pre-breakout detection: Thermometer reading drops to 0.1 * EMA for 3+ bars = exceptionally quiet market, potential breakout imminent. Place straddle or wait for directional break. (2) Trend exhaustion: Thermometer spike > 2 * EMA after strong trend = blow-off top potential, tighten trailing stops. (3) Activity filter: Only enter new positions when thermometer is below EMA (quiet market = better entry prices).
limitations: Two factor parameters (buy_factor, sell_factor) require tuning for each asset. Signal definitions are based on relative comparison to EMA, so absolute levels vary across assets. Buy and sell signals are not standard binary - they represent threshold crossings. Less effective on assets with consistent, steady volatility.

name: Shooting Star
desc: Bearish reversal pattern with a small body at the bottom and a long upper shadow, appearing after an uptrend.
usageContext: Bearish reversal signal appearing after uptrends at resistance. Long upper shadow (2-3x body size) shows buyers pushed price up but sellers rejected higher levels. Small body at bottom (any color, but red stronger) shows closing near low. Opposite of hammer. Requires confirmation (next candle closes lower). Most reliable at resistance levels.
limitations: Must appear in uptrend to be valid - shooting star in downtrend is different pattern (inverted hammer). Needs confirmation from next candle. Upper shadow length threshold subjective. Color matters less than structure, but red preferable. False signals common without resistance confluence. Look-alike to gravestone doji.

name: Vector Crossunder
desc: Crossunder. Returns 1 when the first input crosses below the second input.

name: Forward Returns

options.name: Period
options.desc: Number of periods to look forward
options.tuningGuidance: Period 1 for next bar returns. Larger periods for longer-term forward returns. Common: 1 (next bar), 5 (next week on daily), 20 (next month). Use as target variable for machine learning predictions.

options.name: Return Type
options.desc: Type of return calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Simple returns: (future_price - price) / price. Log returns: log(future_price / price). Log returns are more symmetric and better for ML models. Simple returns are more intuitive for interpretation.

desc: Calculates future returns by looking ahead N periods. For each bar, computes the return from current price to future price. Essential for creating target variables in predictive models.
usageContext: Create target variables for machine learning models predicting future returns. Use as labels for supervised learning — classify future returns into buckets (positive/negative) for direction prediction. Common periods: 1 (next bar), 5 (weekly on daily data), 20 (monthly). Combine with current features to build predictive models. Essential for factor research and alpha discovery workflows.
limitations: Forward-looking transform — last N bars will be null since future data is not available. Cannot be used in live trading for the periods being predicted. Use only for backtesting and model training. Introduces look-ahead bias if used incorrectly in feature engineering.

name: Moving Average

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback period for moving average calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Shorter periods (5-10) for aggressive signals with more noise. Standard 20 for balanced trend detection. Longer periods (50-200) for major trends.

options.name: Type
options.desc: MA calculation method - each type balances responsiveness vs smoothness differently
options.tuningGuidance: SMA: Basic trend and support/resistance. EMA: Standard for trend-following. HMA: Minimize lag. KAMA: Adapts to volatility. DEMA/TEMA: Ultra-responsive. VIDYA: Volatility-adaptive. Wilders: RSI-style smoothing.

desc: Calculates average price over specified period with multiple calculation methods. Acts as a trend indicator and noise filter.
usageContext: Core trend indicator for directional strategies. Use price crossing MA for trend change signals, or dual-MA crossover systems (golden cross: 50 crosses above 200 SMA, death cross: 50 crosses below 200 SMA). MAs act as dynamic support/resistance — price bouncing off MA in a trend confirms strength. Combine with RSI or MACD for confirmation. SMA for support/resistance levels, EMA for trend-following speed, HMA for minimal lag, KAMA/VIDYA for adaptive smoothing in mixed regimes. Use as signal line baseline for custom oscillators (e.g., MACD = EMA(12) - EMA(26)). Trigger phrases: smooth price, trend direction, crossover signal, noise filter.
limitations: All MAs lag price by design — SMA lags most, HMA/DEMA/TEMA least. Shorter periods reduce lag but increase whipsaw frequency. Whipsaws are common in choppy/ranging markets. Not suitable as sole entry signal — combine with volume or momentum filters. Parameter sensitivity: small period changes (e.g., 18 vs 20) can significantly alter signals.

name: Bollinger Bands %B
desc: Measures position within Bollinger Bands as a normalized value between 0 and 1. Values above 1 or below 0 indicate extreme conditions.
usageContext: Use for mean-reversion strategies to identify overbought (%B > 1.0) and oversold (%B < 0.0) conditions. Classic patterns: W-bottom (two dips below 0 with higher second low in %B) signals reversal up; M-top (two pushes above 1 with lower second high in %B) signals reversal down. Combine with bband_width squeeze for anticipating breakouts — narrow width + %B near 0.5 = coiled spring. In strong trends, price 'walks the bands' (%B stays near 1.0 or 0.0 for extended periods) — use RSI divergence for confirmation before fading.
limitations: Less reliable in strong trending markets where price walks the upper or lower band for extended periods. Works best in range-bound conditions. Sensitivity depends on bandwidth (stddev parameter) — wider bands reduce false signals but delay entries.

name: Bar Gap

options.name: Fill Percentage
options.desc: Minimum fill percentage for gap_filled signal
options.tuningGuidance: 100% for complete fill. Lower values for partial fill detection.

options.name: Minimum Gap Size
options.desc: Minimum gap size as percentage to detect. Gaps smaller than this are ignored. Example: 0.04 for 4-pip gaps on EUR/USD.
options.tuningGuidance: Set above typical bid-ask spread to filter noise.

desc: Detects price gaps between any consecutive bars (liquidity gaps, fair value gaps, trading halt gaps) and tracks whether price retraces to fill them. No session boundary requirement.
usageContext: Intraday gap detection between any consecutive bars. Identifies liquidity voids (Fair Value Gaps / FVGs) where price moved so fast that no trading occurred at intermediate levels. Price tends to revisit these gaps to fill the liquidity void. Combine gap_size with volume: large gap + high volume = institutional activity. Use min_gap_size to filter noise gaps smaller than the bid-ask spread.
limitations: More sensitive than session_gap — may generate many signals on volatile instruments. Use min_gap_size filter to reduce noise. Timeframe-dependent: smaller timeframes detect more gaps. Gap fill rates vary by asset class and market conditions.

name: Cross-Sectional Quantile

options.name: Quantile
options.desc: Quantile to compute (0.0-1.0, e.g., 0.25 for 25th percentile)
options.tuningGuidance: 0.25 for lower quartile, 0.5 for median, 0.75 for upper quartile.

options.name: Group By
options.desc: Group assets before applying cross-sectional operation. When set, the transform operates within each group independently.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 'sector' for industry-neutral stock strategies. Use 'category' for futures. Use 'auto_detect' to let the system choose.

desc: Computes a specific quantile across assets at each timestamp. Generalizes median (q=0.5) to any percentile. Uses linear interpolation between data points.
usageContext: Compute specific percentile cutoffs across the asset universe at each timestamp. Generalizes cs_agg(type=Median) to any quantile value. INTERQUARTILE RANGE (IQR): Use q=0.25 and q=0.75 with two cs_quantile instances to compute IQR = Q3 - Q1, a robust measure of cross-sectional spread that is insensitive to outliers (unlike cs_agg(type=Std)). TAIL ANALYSIS: Extreme quantiles (q=0.05, q=0.95) define the boundary of normal behavior. Assets beyond these thresholds are outliers. Plot the 5th/95th quantile time series to monitor tail risk expansion/contraction across the universe. QUANTILE BREAKPOINTS: Use cs_quantile at q=0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 to define quintile boundaries for portfolio sorting (Fama-French style). Assets above the 80th percentile go into quintile 5, assets below 20th into quintile 1. EXAMPLES: (1) Robust cross-sectional spread: IQR = cs_quantile(q=0.75) - cs_quantile(q=0.25). Rising IQR means assets are diverging (stock-pickers market). (2) Tail risk monitor: Plot cs_quantile(q=0.05) and cs_quantile(q=0.95) of daily returns. Widening tails signal increasing market stress.
limitations: Requires multiple assets (5+ recommended for stable quantile estimates). Uses linear interpolation between data points. For median specifically, cs_agg(type=Median) is equivalent to cs_quantile(q=0.5). Extreme quantiles (q<0.1 or q>0.9) need large universes (20+ assets) for stability.

name: Cross-Sectional First/Last

options.name: Group By
options.desc: Group assets before applying cross-sectional operation. When set, the transform operates within each group independently.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 'sector' for industry-neutral stock strategies. Use 'category' for futures. Use 'auto_detect' to let the system choose.

desc: Returns the first and last non-null values across assets at each timestamp as a two-element tuple. Order is determined by the asset/column position in the DataFrame. Outputs: (first_value, last_value).
usageContext: Access boundary values in the cross-section at each timestamp. Outputs a tuple with (first, last) based on column ordering. USE WHEN column order is meaningful: If assets are pre-sorted (e.g., by market cap, by rank, by sector), first/last gives the boundary values. For example, if columns are sorted by market cap descending, first = largest cap value, last = smallest. RANGE COMPUTATION: Combine with math transforms: range = cs_first_last().last - cs_first_last().first to compute the cross-sectional spread when assets are sorted. For unsorted data, prefer cs_agg(type=Min) and cs_agg(type=Max) instead.
limitations: Requires at least 2 assets. Output meaning depends entirely on the column ordering of the input DataFrame. If assets are not pre-sorted, first/last are arbitrary. For min/max regardless of ordering, use cs_agg(type=Min) and cs_agg(type=Max).

name: Mean Deviation Over Period
desc: Mean Deviation Over Period. Calculates the mean deviation over the specified period.
usageContext: Rolling mean absolute deviation - measures average distance from the mean. More robust to outliers than standard deviation. Use as a volatility proxy or for detecting regime changes. PIPELINE PATTERN: compute md(period=20), normalize price deviations by dividing by md. EXAMPLE: rising md signals increasing dispersion and potential trend, falling md signals consolidation.
limitations: Less commonly used than standard deviation in finance. Not directly comparable to stddev (md is ~0.8x stddev for normal distributions). Limited tooling and literature support. Consider stddev for consistency with standard models.

name: Intraday Returns

options.name: Return Type
options.desc: Type of return calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Simple returns: (close - open) / open. Log returns: log(close / open).

desc: Calculates the return from open to close within each bar. Measures intraday price movement.
usageContext: Track the open-to-close return within each bar for intraday momentum strategies. The cumulative intraday return curve reveals momentum patterns — strong early returns that persist suggest institutional flow. Combine with VWAP for execution quality analysis: positive intraday return + price above VWAP = bullish intraday trend.
limitations: Resets each day. Requires session information to determine day boundaries. Single-bar metric — for multi-bar intraday momentum, use returns with appropriate period.

name: Cross-Sectional Labeled Lines - ONE FOR ALL ASSETS

options.name: Chart Title
options.desc: Title for the line chart

options.name: X Axis Label
options.desc: Label for the x-axis

options.name: Y Axis Label
options.desc: Label for the y-axis

options.name: Category
options.desc: Category for grouping in dashboard

options.name: X Axis Labels
options.desc: Category labels for the X axis. Number of labels must match the number of NumericTuple inputs per asset.

options.name: Y Reference Lines
options.desc: Horizontal reference lines on Y axis with optional labels, colors, and dash styles

options.name: Y Axis Format
options.desc: Format type for Y axis values (Auto, Decimal, Percent, Monetary, Integer)

options.name: Y Axis Decimal Places
options.desc: Number of decimal places for Y axis values

options.name: Aggregation
options.desc: Aggregation function for each asset's values per x_label (Last, Mean, Median, etc.)

options.name: Smooth Lines
options.desc: Whether to smooth the lines (spline interpolation)

options.name: Data Labels
options.desc: Show value labels on data points (default: true)

options.name: Line Colors
options.desc: Per-asset line colors (e.g., Blue, Red, Success)

options.name: Asset Filters
options.desc: Filter which assets to display based on ranking criteria. Each filter specifies: rank ('top'/'bottom'), count (number of assets), column (metric to rank by). Chain multiple filters with op ('AND'/'OR').

options.name: Maximum Assets
options.desc: Maximum number of assets to display (0 = no limit). Applied after filters.

options.name: Display Order
options.desc: Display order within dashboard category (lower values appear first, 0 = default position)

desc: Cross-sectional line chart with categorical X axis where each asset becomes a named line. Use for comparing yield curves, factor profiles, or term structures across multiple assets — each asset traces its own curve across the same category labels.
usageContext: TRIGGER PHRASES: Use when the user asks for 'compare yield curves', 'multi-asset term structure', 'factor profiles across assets', 'categorical line comparison', 'overlay term structures'. Plot a LINE CHART with CATEGORICAL X AXIS where EACH ASSET becomes a NAMED LINE. Unlike cs_lines which uses numeric X axis, cs_labeled_lines uses labeled categories like yield curve tenors or factor names. INPUTS: values (NumericTuple) — each asset provides N values, one per x_label. X_LABELS: Required option specifying category names for the X axis (e.g., ['1M', '3M', '6M', '1Y', '2Y', '5Y', '10Y', '30Y']). Number of x_labels must match the number of NumericTuple inputs. AGGREGATION: Each field is aggregated using the 'agg' function (default: Last). COLORS: Per-asset colors via 'colors' option. EXAMPLES: (1) Yield curves by country: x_labels=['1M','1Y','5Y','10Y','30Y'], each country is an asset with its own yield curve line. (2) Factor profiles: x_labels=['Value','Momentum','Quality','Size'], each stock shows its factor exposure profile as a line. (3) Sector exposure: x_labels=['Tech','Finance','Health','Energy'], each fund shows its sector allocation as a line.
limitations: Multi-asset only (isCrossSectional=true). Number of x_labels must match the NumericTuple field count. max_assets defaults to 20. Each asset's series data is reduced via aggregation — temporal detail is lost.

name: Turn of Month

options.name: Days Before Month End
options.desc: Number of trading days before month end to include
options.tuningGuidance: Research suggests 1-2 days before month end. More days may dilute effect.

options.name: Days After Month Start
options.desc: Number of trading days after month start to include
options.tuningGuidance: Research suggests 3-4 days after month start. Test on your specific market.

desc: Detects the turn-of-month calendar anomaly documented by Ariel (1987) and Lakonishok & Smidt (1988). Marks the last N trading days of the month and the first M trading days of the next month. The original research found that all positive DJIA returns over 90 years (1897-1986) occurred within the 4-day window from day -1 to day +3. The effect is attributed to pension fund flows, payroll timing (401k contributions), and institutional rebalancing at month boundaries. Returns during the TOM window average 5-12 basis points per day higher than non-TOM days.

outputs.name: Turn of Month Active (True during TOM window)

usageContext:
Use to exploit the turn-of-month calendar anomaly for timing entries and exits.
- Go long during the TOM window (days_before=1, days_after=3) and exit mid-month for a long-only overlay.
- Use as a position sizing multiplier: increase exposure during TOM, reduce during mid-month.
- Combine with month_of_year to target months with strongest seasonal tailwinds (e.g., November-January).
- Pair with volume analysis (vwap, obv) to confirm institutional flow at month boundaries.
- Strongest in emerging market ETFs (EEM, EWZ) where the effect remains more pronounced.
- Use days_before=2 to capture the anticipatory buying that begins before month-end.
limitations:
The classical 4-day TOM window has weakened significantly in US large-caps since 2010 as the anomaly
became widely known and arbitraged. Requires daily or higher frequency data -- weekly bars cannot capture
the intramonth pattern. Transaction costs (commissions, bid-ask spread) may eliminate the small per-trade
edge. Survivorship bias in historical studies may overstate the effect. The anomaly is stronger in smaller,
less liquid markets but weaker in heavily traded indices like SPY. Not a standalone strategy -- combine
with momentum, mean-reversion, or volatility filters for robustness.

name: Price Profile

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Number of bars for volume profile calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Smaller windows (10-20) for intraday. Larger (50-100) for swing trading.

options.name: Tick Size
options.desc: Price bin granularity
options.tuningGuidance: Match to asset tick size. Smaller = more detail but slower.

options.name: Value Area %
options.desc: Percentage of volume for Value Area (standard is 70%)
options.tuningGuidance: 70% is standard (1 std dev). Use 80% for wider zones, 60% for tighter.

options.name: Profile Mode
options.desc: volume=Volume Profile (volume at price), market=Market Profile (Time Price Opportunity)
options.tuningGuidance: Volume mode aggregates actual volume. TPO mode counts bar touches per level.

options.name: Initial Balance Periods
options.desc: Number of bars for Initial Balance calculation (0=disabled)
options.tuningGuidance: For intraday, use 2 for first hour IB (30min bars). 0 disables IB output.

desc: Rolling Volume/Market Profile analysis. Volume mode computes POC and Value Area based on traded volume. TPO mode (Market Profile) counts time spent at each price level. Optional Initial Balance tracks the range of the first N bars.

outputs.name: Point of Control - price with highest activity

usageContext: Use for identifying fair value (POC), support/resistance (VAH/VAL), and trading zones. Price returning to POC suggests mean reversion. Price outside VA suggests trend/breakout. TPO mode is preferred for intraday analysis. Initial Balance helps identify opening range breakouts.
limitations: Requires volume data for volume mode. Best with liquid instruments. Rolling window introduces lag. POC may not be unique if activity is evenly distributed.

name: Hanging Man
desc: Bearish reversal pattern with a small body at the top and a long lower shadow, appearing in an uptrend. Warning of a potential reversal.
usageContext: Bearish warning signal appearing after uptrends (same structure as hammer but different context). Long lower shadow shows sellers tested lower but buyers defended. However, appears at resistance suggesting exhaustion. Small body at top. Weaker than shooting star - needs strong confirmation. Best when followed by bearish candle closing below hanging man's body.
limitations: Weakest of reversal patterns - requires strong confirmation. Identical to hammer visually - context determines meaning. Can lead to whipsaws. Many hanging men don't lead to reversals. Best used with other bearish indicators. Red body stronger than green. High volume increases reliability. Consider as warning, not entry signal.

name: SuperTrend

options.name: ATR Period
options.desc: Period for Average True Range calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Shorter periods (7-10) for faster signals. Longer (14-21) for smoother trends.

options.name: Multiplier
options.desc: ATR multiplier for band width
options.tuningGuidance: Higher multiplier (3-4) = fewer signals, stronger trends. Lower (1.5-2) = more responsive but more false signals.

desc: Trend-following indicator using ATR-based bands. Flips between upper and lower band based on price breakouts. Provides clear trend direction and trailing stop levels.
usageContext: Use direction changes as trend signals. TradingView standard settings are atr_period=10, multiplier=3. SuperTrend line acts as dynamic support in uptrends and resistance in downtrends. Combine with EMA filter: only take SuperTrend longs when price > EMA(200). For multi-timeframe usage, use higher timeframe SuperTrend for direction and lower timeframe for entries. Parameter optimization: test multiplier 2-4 and atr_period 7-14 grid for each asset class.
limitations: Lags price changes like all trend indicators. Can whipsaw in choppy/ranging markets. Not suitable for range-bound assets — use ADX filter (ADX > 25) to confirm trending conditions. Best combined with other confirmations for entries.

name: Optimal f

options.name: Minimum Trades
options.desc: Minimum trades required before using Optimal f
options.tuningGuidance: 30 (default). Optimal f is more sensitive to small samples than Kelly because it uses the full return distribution and normalizes by worst loss. 50+ recommended for strategies with variable returns.

options.name: Fallback Percent
options.desc: Equity percentage to use when insufficient trade history (10 = 10%)
options.tuningGuidance: 10.0 (default). Same guidance as kelly.fallback_pct — should roughly match expected optimal f allocation to avoid discontinuity at switchover.

options.name: Maximum Leverage
options.desc: Cap on leverage calculated from optimal f / max_loss
options.tuningGuidance: 3.0 (default). 1.0-1.5 for no-leverage accounts (stocks, crypto spot). 5.0 for futures/FX with margin. This is the critical safety cap — without it, optimal f can recommend extreme leverage on favorable return distributions.

desc: Optimal f position sizing (Ralph Vince methodology). Finds the fraction that maximizes geometric growth rate (TWR). Uses full trade return distribution and normalizes by max loss.
usageContext:
Optimal f position sizing based on Ralph Vince's methodology (Vince, 1990). Finds the
fraction of equity to risk that maximizes the Terminal Wealth Relative (TWR) - the geometric
growth rate of the portfolio.

KEY DIFFERENCE FROM KELLY: Kelly uses theoretical parameters (win rate, payoff ratio) and
assumes a Bernoulli distribution. Optimal f uses the FULL EMPIRICAL distribution of trade
returns and normalizes by the worst historical loss. This makes optimal f more responsive
to the actual shape of your return distribution (fat tails, skew, etc.).

TWR MAXIMIZATION: For each candidate fraction f in [0, 1], compute:
TWR = Product(1 + f * return_i / |max_loss|) for all trades i.
The f that maximizes TWR is the optimal f. Position size = (equity * f) / |max_loss|.

MAX_LEVERAGE CAP: Because optimal f can be very aggressive (especially with favorable return
distributions), the max_leverage option caps the effective leverage. Default 3.0 means
allocation never exceeds 300% of equity.

EXAMPLES:
(1) Standard: optimal_f(min_trades=30, max_leverage=3.0)
(2) Conservative: optimal_f(min_trades=50, max_leverage=1.5, fallback_pct=5.0)
(3) Aggressive: optimal_f(min_trades=20, max_leverage=5.0, fallback_pct=15.0)
limitations:
Requires trade history with at least one losing trade (to normalize by max loss). Uses
fallback_pct as a static equity percentage until min_trades completed trades are recorded.
Very aggressive at full optimal f - the max_leverage cap is critical for practical use.
Like Kelly, assumes the future return distribution resembles the historical one. No inputs -
reads from execution context automatically.

name: Chandelier Exit

options.name: Length
options.desc: Period for highest high / lowest low calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Standard is 22. Shorter (10-15) for faster stops. Longer (30-50) for wider stops.

options.name: ATR Length
options.desc: Period for Average True Range calculation
options.tuningGuidance: 14 is standard (Wilder's default). Match to your trading timeframe.

options.name: Multiplier
options.desc: ATR multiplier for stop distance
options.tuningGuidance: Higher (3-4) = wider stops, less whipsaws. Lower (1.5-2) = tighter stops, more sensitive.

options.name: Use Close
options.desc: Use close instead of high/low for stop calculation
options.tuningGuidance: False (default) uses high for long stops, low for short stops. True uses close for both.

desc: ATR-based trailing stop indicator. Long stop = highest high - ATR*mult, Short stop = lowest low + ATR*mult. Direction indicates trend based on price vs stops.
usageContext: Use for trailing stop-loss management based on Chuck LeBeau's original concept. Long stop trails below price in uptrends (highest high - ATR * mult), short stop trails above in downtrends (lowest low + ATR * mult). Direction changes signal trend reversals. Combine with SuperTrend for confirmation — both flipping gives stronger signal. Use for volatility-adjusted position management: wider stops in volatile markets, tighter in calm markets. Standard settings: length=22, atr_length=14, multiplier=2.
limitations: Like all ATR-based stops, can be triggered by volatility spikes (flash crashes, news events). Multiplier sensitivity: too tight triggers frequently, too wide gives back profits. Best used with trend confirmation for entries, not as standalone entry signal.

name: Bars Since
desc: Counts bars elapsed since a boolean condition was last true. Returns 0 when condition fires, increments each subsequent bar. NA if condition has never been true. Use for signal freshness filtering and holding-period tracking.
usageContext: Pine Script ta.barssince() equivalent. Track time decay from signals — use for staleness filtering (barssince(signal) < 5 means signal is fresh), time-based exits (exit after N bars in position), or holding period analysis. Combine with valuewhen to capture entry price then track bars since entry. Common pattern: signal_fresh = barssince(entry_signal) < max_bars_to_enter.
limitations: Returns NA before condition is first true — use coalesce(barssince(cond), 9999) for early bars. Only counts from most recent occurrence.

name: Rolling Covariance

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for covariance calculation (ignored when window_type=expanding)
options.tuningGuidance: Minimum 10-20 bars for stable estimates. Use 20-60 for tactical risk management, 120-252 for strategic portfolio allocation. Larger windows provide smoother estimates but lag regime changes.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative from start)
options.tuningGuidance: Rolling: fixed lookback window, captures recent regime. Expanding: uses all data from start, gives stable full-period covariance.

desc: Calculates covariance between two series over a rolling window. Measures how two variables move together, without normalization like correlation. Units are in product of the input series units.
usageContext: Use for risk management, portfolio optimization, and understanding joint variability. Unlike correlation, covariance preserves magnitude information useful for portfolio variance calculations. Common use: covariance matrix construction for mean-variance optimization, or risk factor analysis where absolute comovement matters. KEY DIFFERENCE from rolling_corr: Covariance preserves scale — output units are product of input units (e.g., %%^2 for return covariance). For normalized [-1,+1] relationship measure comparable across pairs, use rolling_corr instead. Trigger phrases: 'covariance', 'portfolio risk', 'variance contribution', 'risk budgeting', 'covariance matrix', 'joint variability'.
limitations: Not normalized - values depend on input scales, making comparison across different asset pairs difficult. Use rolling_corr for standardized relationship measure. Sensitive to outliers. Requires series to be somewhat stationary for meaningful results.

name: Rising

options.name: Length
options.desc: Number of consecutive rising bars required
options.tuningGuidance: 2-3 for short-term, 5+ for strong trend confirmation

desc: Returns true if the source has been strictly rising (each bar higher than previous — higher-highs) for the specified number of consecutive bars. False if any bar is flat or down.
usageContext: Pine Script ta.rising() equivalent. Confirm uptrend strength by requiring N consecutive higher values. Use as breakout filter: rising(close, 3) after resistance break confirms momentum. Combine with volume: rising(close, 2) && rising(volume, 2) = strong bullish momentum. Good for streak-based entries.
limitations: Requires strict consecutive rises — any flat or down bar breaks the streak. Use length=1 for basic higher-high detection, 3+ for strong confirmation.

name: Johansen Cointegration

options.name: Number of Variables
options.desc: Number of asset price series in the input tuple (2-10).
options.tuningGuidance: Set to match your basket size. 2-3 for pairs/triplets. 4-6 for sector baskets. More variables require proportionally more data (100+ observations per variable).

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for Johansen test. Minimum 100 recommended.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 200+ for reliable eigenvalue estimation. Minimum = 10 * num_vars * lag_p. Longer windows give more stable cointegrating vectors but lag structural breaks.

options.name: VAR Lag Order
options.desc: Lag order for VAR model. Default: 1.
options.tuningGuidance: Lag 1 is standard for daily data. Use 2-4 for intraday or series with strong autocorrelation. Higher lags consume more degrees of freedom.

options.name: Deterministic Order
options.desc: Deterministic specification: -1 (no deterministic), 0 (constant, default), 1 (constant + trend).
options.tuningGuidance: Use 0 (constant) for most financial price series. Use 1 if series have deterministic trends. Use -1 for already-demeaned data.

options.name: Significance Level
options.desc: Significance level for rank determination (default 0.05).

desc: Johansen multivariate cointegration test for 2-10 time series using the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) framework. More powerful than Engle-Granger for multiple series. Returns the cointegration rank (number of independent cointegrating relationships), trace and max eigenvalue statistics, and the cointegrating vector (betas) for spread construction.
usageContext: Test for cointegration among multiple (2-10) time series simultaneously using the Johansen (1988, 1991) VECM approach. More powerful than pairwise Engle-Granger and can find multiple cointegrating relationships. KEY DIFFERENCE from Engle-Granger: (1) Tests all possible cointegrating relationships simultaneously. (2) Not sensitive to variable ordering. (3) Can find multiple independent spreads in a basket. (4) Provides both trace and max eigenvalue test statistics. KEY OUTPUTS: rank = number of cointegrating relationships (0 = no cointegration, 1 = one spread, 2+ = multiple independent spreads). betas = weights for spread construction (spread = betas[0]*X0 + betas[1]*X1 + ...). PIPELINE PATTERN: (1) Pack asset prices into tuple: tuple_pack(asset0, asset1, ..., assetN), (2) run johansen(tuple, num_vars=N, window=200), (3) if rank >= 1, use betas to construct the spread, (4) trade the spread with zscore or half_life_ar1. EXAMPLES: (1) Triangular arbitrage: johansen(tuple_pack(EURUSD, GBPUSD, EURGBP), num_vars=3). Rank=1 confirms the triangular relationship. Betas give optimal hedge weights. (2) Sector basket: johansen on 5 energy stocks. Rank=2 means two independent cointegrating relationships exist - construct and trade both spreads. (3) ETF arbitrage: johansen(tuple_pack(SPY, IVV, VOO), num_vars=3). Should have rank=2 (all three track S&P 500).
limitations: Computationally intensive - O(n^3) in number of variables per window. Requires sufficient data: minimum 10 * num_vars * lag_p observations per window. Eigenvalue estimation can be unstable with near-zero eigenvalues. The trace and max eigenvalue tests may disagree - prefer trace test for practical purposes. Critical values depend on number of variables and deterministic specification. Johansen syntax: johansen(tuple_pack(asset0, asset1, ...), num_vars=N, window=100)

name: Linear Decay
desc: Linear Decay. Applies linear decay to each element in the input over the specified period.
usageContext: Applies linearly decreasing weight to signal values over a lookback period. Useful for decaying event flags or signal strength over time. A signal of 1.0 decays to 0.0 over the period. PIPELINE PATTERN: generate binary signal, then apply decay to create a fading weight. EXAMPLE: decay(period=5) on a buy signal produces weights [1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2] for position sizing.
limitations: Linear decay is simplistic compared to exponential decay. Output reaches zero exactly at the period boundary. Not suitable for signals requiring smooth asymptotic decay. Consider edecay for more natural decay curves.

name: Momentum
desc: Momentum. Measures rate of change in prices by comparing current price to a previous price.
usageContext: Raw price change: current price minus price n periods ago. Simplest momentum measure. Positive = price higher than n bars ago, negative = lower. Zero-crossings signal trend changes. Magnitude shows momentum strength. PIPELINE PATTERN: compute mom(period=10), use zero crossovers for trend direction. EXAMPLE: mom turning positive = price now above where it was 10 bars ago, momentum shifting bullish.
limitations: Absolute values - not normalized across instruments (use roc for %). Sensitive to the single bar n periods ago (comparison point). Can give false signals when the comparison bar was unusual. Noisy without smoothing. Consider roc for percentage-based momentum.

name: Quantitative Qualitative Estimation (QQE)

options.name: RSI Average Period
options.desc: Period for the underlying RSI calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 14 for most applications. Use 5-8 for faster signals on intraday charts. Use 21-30 for smoother, less frequent signals.

options.name: Smoothing Period
options.desc: EMA smoothing period applied to RSI for signal line
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 5. Higher values create smoother but more lagging signals. Lower values for faster, noisier signals.

options.name: Width Factor
options.desc: Multiplier for the ATR-like volatility bands around the smoothed RSI
options.tuningGuidance: Default 4.236 (Fibonacci). Higher values widen the bands, producing fewer but stronger signals. Lower values for more frequent signals.

desc: Smoothed RSI-based indicator with dynamic volatility bands. Combines RSI with ATR-like volatility envelope to generate cleaner trend signals than raw RSI. Returns smoothed RSI, RSI moving average, and long/short signal lines.
usageContext: Advanced RSI-based trend indicator that reduces noise through double smoothing and adds dynamic volatility bands for signal generation. Developed to overcome RSI's tendency to produce false signals in trending markets. KEY SIGNALS: (1) QQE line crosses above RSI MA = bullish momentum, (2) QQE line crosses below RSI MA = bearish momentum. (3) Long line provides dynamic support - when QQE holds above it, trend is intact. (4) Short line provides dynamic resistance. PIPELINE PATTERN: (1) Compute QQE with default parameters, (2) enter long when QQE crosses above long_line from below (bullish breakout), (3) hold while QQE stays above long_line, (4) exit when QQE drops below long_line. Reverse for shorts using short_line. KEY DIFFERENCE from raw RSI: QQE's double smoothing + volatility bands eliminate most of RSI's whipsaw signals. The width_factor (default 4.236, a Fibonacci multiple) controls signal sensitivity. EXAMPLES: (1) Trend entry: QQE crosses above 50 AND above long_line = strong bullish confirmation. Enter long with stop below recent swing low. (2) Divergence: Price making higher highs but QQE making lower highs = bearish divergence, potential trend exhaustion. (3) Multi-indicator: Combine QQE trend direction with Alligator alignment for high-probability entries.
limitations: Multiple smoothing operations create significant lag - not suitable for scalping. Three parameters (avg_period, smooth_period, width_factor) can be over-optimized. Default 4.236 Fibonacci factor is somewhat arbitrary. In strong trends, QQE may stay above/below signal lines for extended periods, giving no exit signal. Less effective in ranging markets where signals cluster around the center.

name: Highest Bars

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback period to search for highest value
options.tuningGuidance: 260 for 52-week high, 20 for monthly high

desc: Returns how many bars ago the highest value occurred within the lookback period. 0 means current bar is the high (new high / breakout). Negative values indicate bars ago (-5 = high was 5 bars ago).
usageContext: Pine Script ta.highestbars() equivalent. Detect how recently a new high was made — highestbars == 0 means new high on current bar (breakout). Use for breakout freshness: highestbars(high, 260) == 0 detects 52-week highs. Momentum timing: compare highestbars offset between price and indicator for divergence detection.
limitations: Returns NA for first (period-1) bars. Only tracks the most recent highest — does not capture multiple highs within the lookback.

name: Aroon
desc: Aroon. Measures the time between highs and lows over a time period, identifying trends and corrections.
usageContext: Two lines: Aroon Up and Aroon Down (0-100). Measures time since highest high / lowest low in period. Up above 70 & Down below 30 = strong uptrend. Down above 70 & Up below 30 = strong downtrend. Both below 50 = consolidation. Crossovers signal trend changes. Better at identifying trend beginnings than ADX. Default 25 period.
limitations: Based solely on time since highs/lows, ignores price magnitude. Can give early signals before trend established. Consolidation periods (both low) ambiguous. Requires confirmation from other indicators. Less popular than ADX. Works best on trending instruments with clear swings.

name: Percent Rank

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback period for percentile calculation
options.tuningGuidance: 50-100 for relative volume, 252 for annual percentile

desc: Returns the percentile rank (0-100) of the current value relative to all values in the lookback period. 100 = highest, 0 = lowest.
usageContext: Pine Script ta.percentrank() equivalent. Normalize any indicator to 0-100 scale relative to its own history. Great for relative volume detection (percentrank(volume, 50) > 90 = top 10% volume in last 50 bars), percentile-based thresholds instead of fixed values, and making indicators comparable across assets with different scales.
limitations: This is time-series percentile (vs own history). Use cs_rank_quantile for cross-sectional ranking (vs other assets). Sensitive to lookback period — short periods amplify noise, long periods smooth too much.

name: Hold Until
desc: Converts pulse signals to continuous held signal. Sets output to True when enter signal fires, maintains True until exit signal fires. Essential for using discrete crossover/crossunder signals with zone-based executors like long_zone().
usageContext: Use when you have discrete entry/exit signals (like crossover/crossunder) but want to use long_zone() or short_zone() executors. The held signal stays True for the entire duration of the position. Example: long_zone()(hold_until()(crossover(close, st), crossunder(close, st)))
limitations: If both enter and exit signals are True on the same bar, enter takes priority (position is maintained). For opposite behavior, swap the signal order or use additional logic. Null inputs preserve current state — they don't reset the hold.

name: Moving Average Convergence/Divergence
desc: Moving Average Convergence/Divergence. Trend-following momentum indicator showing relationship between two moving averages.
usageContext: Combines trend and momentum in one indicator. Three components: MACD line (12-26 EMA diff), Signal line (9 EMA of MACD), Histogram (MACD - Signal). Signals: MACD crosses Signal (bullish/bearish), histogram expansion/contraction (momentum strength), divergence (price vs MACD disagreement). Use for trend confirmation and entry timing.
limitations: Lagging indicator based on EMAs. Default 12/26/9 parameters may not suit all timeframes or assets. Can give false signals in ranging markets. Histogram can be misleading during consolidation. Works best in trending markets. Requires parameter optimization for different instruments.

name: K-Means Clustering

options.name: Number of Clusters
options.desc: Number of clusters (K)

options.name: Max Iterations
options.desc: Maximum Lloyd's algorithm iterations. 1000 is usually sufficient for convergence.

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Size of training window (for rolling) or minimum window (for expanding)
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default): ~1 year of daily data. Use 126 (~6 months) for faster adaptation to regime changes but less training data. Use 504 (~2 years) for more stable models at the cost of slower adaptation. Rule of thumb: window should contain at least 10x the number of features. For intraday bars, scale proportionally.

options.name: Retrain Frequency
options.desc: How often to retrain: 21 = 21 bars, 1M = monthly, 1Y = yearly, 1W = weekly
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default): Retrain monthly on daily data. Use 1 for every-bar retraining (expensive but most adaptive). Use 63 (quarterly) for slow-changing models. Duration syntax: '1M' = calendar month, '1W' = week, '21' = 21 bars. More frequent retraining = higher computational cost but faster adaptation.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling uses fixed-size window; Expanding grows from start
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default): Fixed-size training window that slides forward. Model sees only recent data, adapts to regime changes, but forgets old patterns. expanding: Training window grows from start (GKX 2020 methodology). Model sees all historical data, more stable but slower to adapt. Use expanding for long-term factor models; rolling for tactical/short-horizon strategies.

options.name: Min Training Samples
options.desc: Minimum samples required before first prediction
options.tuningGuidance: 100 (default): Reasonable minimum for most models. For LightGBM, use 200+ for stable tree construction. For logistic regression, 50 may suffice. Rule of thumb: min_training_samples >= 10 * num_features. Lower values start predictions sooner but risk unreliable early predictions.

desc: K-Means clustering with rolling/expanding window training. Retrains centroids as new data arrives for adaptive regime detection.
usageContext: Use for adaptive regime detection where cluster definitions evolve over time.
limitations: Higher computational cost. Clusters may shift between windows.

name: Calendar Shift

options.name: Period
options.desc: Calendar duration to shift. Positive = backward (lag), negative = forward (lead). Examples: 63D, 1M, 1W.
options.tuningGuidance: Use calendar durations instead of bar counts when comparing across assets with different trading calendars. 63D = ~1 quarter, 1M = ~21 trading days, 1W = ~5 trading days.

desc: Shifts a series by a calendar duration rather than a fixed number of bars. For each bar at time T, returns the value at the most recent bar at or before (T - duration). Ensures consistent calendar-based lookback across assets with different trading calendars.
usageContext: Use instead of positional lag (>> N) when reference data must produce identical values across multiple assets with different trading calendars. Essential for multi-asset event studies where a shared signal (oil return, VIX level, DXY move) should fire identically across all assets.
limitations: Requires time-based duration, not bar count. Uses backward asof matching — if no bar exists at or before the target date, returns null. For bar-based shifting, use the standard lag transform (>> operator).

name: Fair Value Gap

options.name: Join Consecutive Gaps
options.desc: Merge adjacent/overlapping FVGs into larger zones
options.tuningGuidance: True (default) = cleaner chart with merged zones, better for slower timeframes. False = all individual FVGs shown, useful for scalping/precision entries.

desc: Identifies Fair Value Gaps (FVG) where price makes a significant move leaving an empty zone that often gets filled later, signaling potential reversal zones.
usageContext: SMC concept: price imbalance zones where market moved too fast, leaving 'gaps' between candle bodies. Price often returns to fill these zones (mitigation). Bullish FVG = support zone, Bearish FVG = resistance.
limitations: Not all FVGs get filled - some remain unfilled in strong trends. Mitigation can be partial. Works better on liquid instruments. Intraday FVGs less reliable than higher timeframe FVGs.

name: Kalman Filter

options.name: Model Type
options.desc: Pre-built state-space model type

options.name: Process Noise
options.desc: Process noise variance Q. Higher = state changes faster

options.name: Observation Noise
options.desc: Observation noise variance R. Higher = trust state more than observations

options.name: Initial State Covariance
options.desc: Initial state uncertainty. Higher = learn faster from early observations

options.name: Confidence Level
options.desc: Confidence level for uncertainty bounds

desc: State-space filter for extracting hidden states from noisy observations. Useful for trend extraction, noise reduction, and dynamic parameter estimation.

outputs.name: Filtered level estimate (hidden state). Use as denoised signal.
Upper confidence bound for level estimate.
Lower confidence bound for level estimate.
Variance of level estimate. Lower = more confident.
Filtered trend/velocity estimate (2nd state, if applicable).
Upper confidence bound for trend estimate.
Lower confidence bound for trend estimate.

usageContext: Use for denoising time series, extracting hidden trends, or building adaptive trading models. The ratio process_noise/obs_noise controls filter responsiveness.
limitations: Assumes linear state dynamics and Gaussian noise. For non-linear models, use extended or unscented Kalman filters.

name: Liquidity

options.name: Range Percentage
options.desc: Maximum distance between swing points to be considered a cluster (as % of price)
options.tuningGuidance: 0.001 (0.1%) for stocks/forex. Adjust based on instrument volatility - lower for tight clusters, higher for broader zones. Too low = miss clusters, too high = false clusters.

desc: Identifies clusters of swing highs or lows that are close to each other, representing areas where significant buyer/seller liquidity is present.
usageContext: SMC liquidity pools concept: clusters of swing points where stop losses accumulate. 'Smart money' sweeps these levels to trigger stops before reversing. Use to anticipate stop hunts and reversal zones.
limitations: Requires swing_highs_lows input. Not all liquidity pools get swept. Sweep timing unpredictable. Works best on liquid markets where stop hunting is common (forex, futures, major stocks).

name: Order Blocks

options.name: Use Close for Mitigation
options.desc: Require candle close in OB zone for mitigation, not just wick
options.tuningGuidance: False (default) = wick touch mitigates OB, more sensitive. True = require close inside OB, more conservative. Use true on higher timeframes to avoid premature mitigation.

desc: Detects bullish and bearish order blocks which represent areas of significant institutional order flow, often acting as support and resistance zones.
usageContext: SMC cornerstone: the last opposing candle before strong move = institutional order accumulation zone. Bullish OB = last down candle before rally (buy zone). Bearish OB = last up candle before drop (sell zone). Price often retraces to OBs before continuing trend.
limitations: Requires swing_highs_lows input. Not all OBs hold - some get breached in strong momentum. Volume data improves accuracy but not always available. Best on trending markets - less reliable in ranges.

name: Economic Indicators

options.name: Series ID
options.desc: FRED series ID (e.g., CPIAUCSL, UNRATE) or EIA series ID (e.g., WCESTUS1, RWTC) when eia_route is set

options.name: EIA API Route
options.desc: EIA API route (e.g., 'petroleum/stoc/wstk', 'natural-gas/stor/wkly'). When set, fetches from EIA instead of FRED

options.name: EIA Frequency
options.desc: EIA data frequency: Weekly, Monthly, Annual, Daily. Only used when eia_route is set

desc: Load macro and energy data (FRED + EIA) for analysis. Data is indexed by observation date (the measurement period). Use for regime detection, risk-on/risk-off, and macro analysis. Access any FRED series by ID, or any EIA series by providing eia_route + series_id. Use for specialized indicators not in the common list.
usageContext: The DataFrame index is the observation date. Use for regime detection, risk-on/risk-off, and macro analysis. Example: economic_indicators(series_id="WALCL")().result for Fed balance sheet. For daily market data: economic_indicators(series_id="DCOILWTICO")().
limitations: Publication frequency varies: daily (rates/VIX), weekly (claims/oil), monthly (CPI/employment/natgas), quarterly (GDP). Values appear on observation dates. Data is US-centric. Series ID must be valid FRED series. Check https://fred.stlouisfed.org to find available series.

name: Rate of Change Ratio
desc: Rate of Change Ratio. Calculates the ratio of current price to price n periods ago, measuring momentum.
usageContext: Price ratio: current_price / price_n_periods_ago. ROCR > 1.0 = price higher, < 1.0 = lower. Multiplicative version of ROC. Useful for compounding momentum across periods. PIPELINE PATTERN: compute rocr(period=12), values above 1.0 indicate positive momentum. EXAMPLE: rocr = 1.10 means price is 10% above where it was n periods ago.
limitations: Less intuitive than percentage-based ROC. Oscillates around 1.0 instead of 0, making threshold setting different. Same single-bar comparison sensitivity as ROC. Use roc for percentage interpretation.

name: ML Robust

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Size of training window (for rolling) or minimum window (for expanding)
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default): ~1 year of daily data. Use 126 (~6 months) for faster adaptation to regime changes but less training data. Use 504 (~2 years) for more stable models at the cost of slower adaptation. Rule of thumb: window should contain at least 10x the number of features. For intraday bars, scale proportionally.

options.name: Retrain Frequency
options.desc: How often to retrain: 21 = 21 bars, 1M = monthly, 1Y = yearly, 1W = weekly
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default): Retrain monthly on daily data. Use 1 for every-bar retraining (expensive but most adaptive). Use 63 (quarterly) for slow-changing models. Duration syntax: '1M' = calendar month, '1W' = week, '21' = 21 bars. More frequent retraining = higher computational cost but faster adaptation.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling uses fixed-size window; Expanding grows from start
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default): Fixed-size training window that slides forward. Model sees only recent data, adapts to regime changes, but forgets old patterns. expanding: Training window grows from start (GKX 2020 methodology). Model sees all historical data, more stable but slower to adapt. Use expanding for long-term factor models; rolling for tactical/short-horizon strategies.

options.name: Min Training Samples
options.desc: Minimum samples required before first prediction
options.tuningGuidance: 100 (default): Reasonable minimum for most models. For LightGBM, use 200+ for stable tree construction. For logistic regression, 50 may suffice. Rule of thumb: min_training_samples >= 10 * num_features. Lower values start predictions sooner but risk unreliable early predictions.

desc: Robust normalization with rolling/expanding window training using median and IQR. Less sensitive to outliers than z-score or min-max scaling.
usageContext: Use when data contains outliers that would distort z-score or min-max normalization. Robust scaling uses median and IQR (interquartile range) instead of mean and standard deviation, making it resilient to extreme values. Best default choice for financial data which typically has fat tails. PIPELINE PATTERN: tuple_pack(features) → ml_robust → lightgbm_classifier/regressor. Trigger phrases: 'robust normalization', 'outlier-resistant scaling', 'median-IQR scaling', 'fat-tail preprocessing'.
limitations: Requires more samples (50+) for stable median/IQR estimation. Less interpretable than z-score (output is not in standard deviation units).

Use 504 (~2 years) for more stable models at the cost of slower adaptation. Rule of thumb: window should contain at least 10x the number of features. For intraday bars, scale proportionally.

options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default): Retrain monthly on daily data. Use 1 for every-bar retraining (expensive but most adaptive). Use 63 (quarterly) for slow-changing models. Duration syntax: '1M' = calendar month, '1W' = week, '21' = 21 bars. More frequent retraining = higher computational cost but faster adaptation.

options.desc: Rolling uses fixed-size window; Expanding grows from start
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default): Fixed-size training window that slides forward. Model sees only recent data, adapts to regime changes, but forgets old patterns. expanding: Training window grows from start (GKX 2020 methodology). Model sees all historical data, more stable but slower to adapt. Use expanding for long-term factor models; rolling for tactical/short-horizon strategies.
